products.description: Build an AI business case from your explicit operating and cost assumptions. Compare low, base and high scenarios, recovered capacity, cash flow, NPV and payback. Explore editable project-cost assumptions. Results support planning; they are not a quote or financial advice.
products.audience: Product, operations and transformation leaders comparing a defined AI investment.
products.skillDescription: Build or revise a defined AI business case with explicit assumptions, separate cash and capacity, and low, base and high scenarios.
workflow: Clarify the use case and decision. Collect users, minutesPerTask, tasksPerUserPerMonth, low/base/high savings fractions, hourlyCost, buildCost, monthlyRunCost, adoptionMonths, horizonMonths, annualDiscountRate, cashRealisation and a three-letter currency. Ask for missing assumptions or offer clearly labelled editable assumptions for the user to confirm; do not silently fill factual gaps.

Call estimate_ai_roi with those explicit inputs. Report hours of recoverable capacity separately from realised cash benefits. A cashRealisation of zero means no cash benefit, even when staff time is released. Show all three scenarios, NPV, payback (including unavailable payback) and the assumptions driving them.

For a requested proof-of-concept, pilot or production budget, call estimate_ai_project_cost with stage and any supplied people, durationWeeks, dayRate and currency. Explain that defaults are planning assumptions rather than a supplier quote. Do not substitute that estimate for the user's actual agreed build cost without confirmation.

When the inputs are complete, call show_ai_business_case with the same ROI inputs to show the interactive result. Recalculate after an agreed assumption changes. Explain the result in relation to the user's decision; do not guarantee savings, approve an investment or claim independent financial advice.

products.description: Run an evidence-led AI readiness self-assessment using 30 anchored questions across six dimensions. See scores, response coverage and gaps. Maturity bands require at least 80% response coverage. This supports internal self-assessment, not certification.
products.audience: Leaders and teams assessing a defined organisational scope before an AI initiative.
products.skillDescription: Run or revise an AI readiness self-assessment from explicit question responses and evidence; show coverage and unanswered areas.
workflow: Agree the team, business unit and period being assessed. Fetch the versioned questionnaire with assess_ai_readiness using {"mode":"questionnaire"}. Use its exact question IDs and anchored 1-5 scores. Let the user work through relevant sections in manageable groups.

Capture only explicitly supplied questionId, score and optional evidence. Ask the user to resolve ambiguous responses. Leave unanswered questions absent rather than guessing a score from the general conversation.

Call assess_ai_readiness using {"responses":{"answers":[...]}} and any explicitly agreed dimension weights. Show response coverage alongside scores. Preserve withheld bands when coverage is below 80%, and distinguish unanswered evidence from low scores.

Call show_ai_readiness with the same assessment inputs for the interactive result. Prioritise practical evidence gaps in the supplied scope. State that this framework is self-assessment support; it does not certify compliance or replace an independent workflow audit.

products.description: Prioritise supplied AI use cases using explicit value, feasibility, ownership and indicative governance gates. Inspect dependencies and outcome measures before taking an idea forward. The app does not certify legal risk or approve deployment.
products.audience: Portfolio, product and transformation teams comparing a supplied list of AI initiatives.
products.skillDescription: Compare a supplied AI use-case list with explicit value, feasibility, ownership and governance gates; preserve missing facts.
workflow: Collect the use cases the user wants to compare. For each, obtain id, title, problem, ownerRole, businessUnit, value and feasibility from 0 to 5, riskTier and status. Keep unknown risk as unknown. Record supplied dependencies, data sensitivity, outcome KPIs and assumptions when available.

Call generate_usecase_register with {"useCases":[...]}. Governance gates precede numeric priority: prohibited uses are blocked, and high or unknown risk requires review. A value-times-feasibility score is a prioritisation aid, not permission to deploy.

Call show_ai_usecase_priorities with the same explicit register input. Explain the score and gate for each option, dependencies and the next evidence needed. Do not fabricate initiatives, owners, approvals, customer evidence or legal conclusions.

When the user changes a value, feasibility or risk assumption, confirm that change and rerun the tools. Keep the difference between a proposed decision and an authorised organisational decision clear.

products.description: Connect supplied teams, OKRs, roadmap outcomes and interactions into an explainable product operating model. Inspect missing ownership and dependency checks. products.audience: Product and delivery leaders planning responsibilities and outcomes across defined teams.

workflow: Collect the teams in scope with stable id, name, type and size. Team types are stream-aligned, platform, enabling or complicated-subsystem. Add supplied products, measurable OKRs, roadmap items and interactions when relevant; ask for missing facts rather than inventing organisational records.

For each key result, collect id, description, baseline, target, current and confidence. Add accountable team IDs when supplied. Roadmap items need an id, title and now/next/later horizon; capture their intended outcome and team/OKR links. Interactions identify from, to and collaboration, X-as-a-Service or facilitating mode.

Call generate_operating_model with the explicit model. Explain ownership, dependency and outcome checks using the supplied facts. Decreasing targets are valid; do not silently reverse them. Keep unknown links visible.

Call show_product_operating_model with the same input to present the model and checks. Team Topologies is a referenced framework, with no affiliation implied. The checks support a design conversation rather than determine staffing, approve budgets or mandate a reorganisation.

products.description: Prepare a vendor-neutral AI procurement pack from a defined buying brief. Select evidence questions, must-have criteria and blank supplier response worksheets. Call build_ai_procurement_pack with the title, brief and supplied optional sector, criteria, mustHaveCriteria and suppliers. Use documented criterion IDs from the tool schema/reference. Keep must-have requirements distinct from scored questions. The buyer confirms requirement choices. Preserve blank supplier answers, evidence and scores until actual supplier responses are supplied and a separate authorised evaluation is requested. Do not populate the sheet with Tenhaw marketing claims or any other vendor's invented credentials.

Call show_ai_procurement_pack with the same confirmed inputs to display the pack. Explain that sector prompts and contract questions support the buyer's procurement, security and legal review; they do not certify legal compliance or award a contract. The authored question framework is CC BY 4.0; retain its applicable attribution when exporting.
